lens: Neo-brutalism (Gumroad style): thick borders, loud flat colors, unapologetic typography
name: Loud Dial Neo-Brutal
one_liner: A loud, ink-bordered sales cockpit: each live call is a stamped, coached scorecard, and the persona library reads like a deck of trading cards.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Gumroad lens: 3px ink borders on every container and control, hard 4px offset shadows, flat loud fills (yellow, pink, mint, blue, orange) and heavy uppercase display type. Changed three things. (1) A calm paper reading mode for transcripts and debriefs, because dense quotes need legibility. (2) A dark Night Shift variant for live calls. (3) shadcn/ui primitives instead of hand-rolled classes, so contributors get accessible parts. Research: Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli and Mindtickle all ship enterprise blue-and-white, so loud neo-brutal is a real differentiator. Mobbin live-call hits were weak (chat and meeting UIs); the Delphi transcript and the Shopify voice overlay were closest. Self-scores: A 8, B 7, C 8.5.

design_language.typography: Archivo variable (width 112 to 125, weight 800 to 900), uppercase display with -0.02em tracking: 88px hero, 40px H2, 22px card titles. Inter 400 and 500 at 16px with 1.6 line height for transcripts. JetBrains Mono 600 for timers, scores and weights. Rule: ink text on every loud fill; never white on yellow, mint, pink or orange.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 3px solid ink border on every card, button, input and chip. Radius 12px on cards, pill radius on chips. Depth is a hard 4px offset shadow in ink, with no blur and no gradients. Pressed state moves the element 2px and shrinks the shadow to 2px. Long reading surfaces drop to 1px hairlines.
design_language.motion: Snap, not float. 120ms press, 200ms whisper cue slide-in from the right, 280ms score stamp (scale 0.8 to 1.06 to 1), live meters step in eight notches. Reduced-motion removes transforms and keeps colour changes.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 20px, stroke 2.5, set inside 36px ink-bordered squares. No emoji in product UI. Persona avatars are flat geometric illustrations with 3px outlines, colour-keyed by industry.
design_language.theme_modes: Daylight (default) on paper. Night Shift dark for live calls and the wizard, auto-set from the OS and switchable. Both modes pass WCAG AA for text. The app is light-only today, so this is new work, but it is cheap once tokens live on :root.

navigation_and_ia: Top bar: an ink-bordered logo block and four chunky tabs: Practice, Library, Progress, Team (Team appears only with an org). Cmd+K opens persona search. Starting a call swaps the top bar for a 48px rec strip with timer and End and grade. The wizard is reached from a Library 'Build a persona' tile and from the empty state. Mobile uses a bottom tab bar with the same four tabs. Account, MFA and settings sit under the avatar menu.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Per-turn pipeline: each rep turn triggers a coach call and a grader call, using separate prompts. The UI shows one whisper cue at a time (10s lifetime; the Used tick logs adherence), an orange objection stripe, a six-step talk-track rail that ticks as evidence lands, and five live criterion bars that stamp up or down, hatched until a transcript quote confirms them. It also shows a talk-ratio meter and a coach latency chip. Target: a cue visible under 1.5s after the caller finishes. Self-score D: 6.0. The design meets the baseline and exceeds it on visibility. Brilliance depends on latency and grader accuracy, which the UI cannot fix.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: a target of 200+ seeded personas, stored as JSON in the repo, across the brief's 15 sales jobs. Filters: sales job, industry, difficulty (Easy, Medium, Hard, Brutal), objection type (price, timing, competitor, authority, no need) and voice. Every persona ships with an objection set, talk track and rubric template, so each card is a complete scenario. Wizard: six steps and five input sources (job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP fields, pasted call). The persona card fills live from streamed output, a 60-second test call runs before save, and the result exports as a persona file for a community PR. Self-score E: 6.5. Seeded content quality is the real risk.
signature_moments: Score stamp: a criterion bar slams with a hard shadow when evidence lands.
Whisper cue cards: yellow sticky notes that tilt, then peel off when marked Used.
Persona trading cards with difficulty stamps and objection badges, which feel collectible.
'Replay this line': each debrief quote jumps the transcript and flashes the matching line.
Wizard persona card that assembles field by field, with a yellow flash on each update.
Press-down CTAs: the hard shadow collapses on click, the signature Gumroad gesture.
openai_fund_angle: Visible, not footnoted. The live call shows the model behind each function: a voice engine (OpenAI Realtime added beside ElevenLabs), a fast coach model, a GPT-4.1-mini grader and a larger model for the debrief. Each cue and score carries a model chip with latency and cost in cents. Settings gets a model router with one dropdown per function. The wizard button reads 'Generate with GPT'. For contributors, 'Contribute a persona' drafts the file with Codex CLI and opens a PR; community PRs carry a 'Reviewed with Codex' badge, and the footer reads 'Built with Codex'. Business viability (self-scored): F1 SaaS 6, since Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli and Mindtickle already sell AI roleplay, so differentiate on real-call coaching. F2 licensing 7, since the persona library and wizard are sellable IP for call centres and training firms. F3 'not worth building' 3, so it is worth building.

shadcn-based neo-brutal border and shadow recipes, used as reference for our tokens.

implementation.migration_path: 1) Tokens and shell: Tailwind theme (borders, hard shadows, palette), Archivo and JetBrains Mono fonts, shadcn copy-in, restyled top bar. 2) Practice flow: pre-call and live call behind a feature flag, with coach and per-turn scorer endpoints. 3) Debrief and progress views. 4) Persona library: seed 200+ JSON personas, filters, grid. 5) Wizard. 6) Manager view and mobile QA. Keep the existing routes and localStorage scenarios, and map them to the new persona file format.

risks: Neo-brutalism can read as playful or consumer-grade to enterprise buyers. Mitigate with dense data type, the paper reading mode, and loud colour on roughly a fifth of the surface.
Ink borders and hard shadows on every element add visual noise, which hurts long debriefs. Limit hard shadows to controls and top-level cards.
Contrast: loud fills need ink text. Any light text on yellow, pink, mint or orange fails AA, so run a token audit before building.
Coach latency decides whether live cues feel real. The UI cannot hide a slow model, so budget under 1.5s.
Seeded persona quality (200+ personas with objection sets) is content work. Weak objection sets would make the library look thin even with a strong UI.
Copy-in shadcn means the project owns its components. Contributors must learn the repo's tokens rather than install a package.
